title_en: Two-Track Safety-Gated Inference: A Public-Safe Falsification Architecture for Meaning-Driven Signals
abstract_en_180w: Two-Track Safety-Gated Inference: A Public-Safe Falsification Architecture for Meaning-Driven Signals proposes a safety-gated evaluation architecture for meaning-rich cross-reference signals that are expressive but vulnerable to overfitting when promoted directly to trading actions. We separate K-track (knowledge/IP narrative generation) from T-track (survivor filtering, rollback contracts, and operational gates), and validate claims with multi-baseline comparison, raw OOS readiness checks, and bootstrap/permutation significance. Current gate status is bundle_ready=True, ready_for_publication_claim=True, with falsification pass 5/5. Robustness sensitivity reports first non-pass at min_survivor_count=7 and min_ci_low_defense_contrib=0.0. A fail-boundary layer defines max-safe survivor floor=5 and first-break threshold=7, which is wired to an explicit no-go gate. Public disclosure remains redacted at formula/weight level, while reproducibility is preserved through artifact-chain checkpoints.
contributions_en: Two-track architecture that separates narrative insight generation from execution gating.
Falsification-first validation with explicit fail-boundary and rollback semantics.
Public-safe disclosure strategy with artifact-chain reproducibility for applied review.
